correctness.rationale: For each mutant-resident edge, opposite reproduction events cancel in the expected change of inverse-degree weighted mutant mass, proving the fixation probability formula. The first-step moment equation (I-Q)u=h is derived with the fixation indicator and includes no-change updates. All nine connected graph isomorphism classes through order four have transitive degree classes. Exhaustive exact-Fraction enumeration of 21 classes at order five finds precisely 7 classes with same-probability seeds but distinct conditional means. A separately constructed 14-state interval transition chain reproduces the exact P5 fractions 14650/329 and 26955/658 and positive difference 335/94. Both standalone programs pass and check rational-system residuals.

evidence: Hindersin et al. (2015) provide general exact transition-matrix methods which could compute the claimed census but do not state its exact seven-class five-vertex outcome.
Möller–Hindersin–Traulsen (2019) enumerate graph classes and describe graph-averaged observables, not equal-probability vertices within each graph.
Brewster et al. (2026) treat mixed updating rules and bounds, rather than this fixed neutral birth–death seed equivalence.
McAvoy–Hauert (2015) proves general symmetry results and supplies a 12-vertex regular graph as a nonequivalence example, but not a five-vertex sharp cutoff or order-five census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An algorithm capable of deriving an exact census does not, by itself, assert the census. Inspected broader settings had either other objectives, aggregate graph observables, or different update mechanisms; no theorem found logically forces the stated exact count and sharpness. The closest earlier counterexample is strictly larger, and its statements do not determine the minimum of all connected unweighted networks.

evidence: Sood–Antal–Redner proves the success-probability identity, which does not constrain the conditional first moment.
Hindersin–Traulsen studies conditional fixation-time variation, but its explicit small-graph layer is four-vertex rather than the new order-five classification.
Mohamadichamgavi–Miękisz (2024) discusses dependence on seed degree using large random graphs and mean-field approximations, not an exact graph-order cutoff.
McAvoy–Hauert states the broad qualitative phenomenon and conditional-fixation-time analogue; it does not claim five vertices are minimal or list seven five-vertex graph classes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known success probabilities plus general time recursions allow recomputation, not a direct logical implication of a sharp five-vertex minimum or a seven-class classification. Neither a same-subject title nor absence of a search hit is treated as a proof of priority. Thus the generic difference between success probability and conditional fixation time is not novel, whereas the sharp minimal-size and complete first-layer exact count remain the distinct claims.

evidence: Sood–Antal–Redner (2007/2008) gives the neutral invasion fixation probability in terms of inverse degree, making equal probabilities equivalent to equal degrees in this setting.
Hindersin–Traulsen (2014) analyzes location-dependent fixation times and all six connected four-vertex graph types, not the order-five seven-class distinction.
McAvoy–Hauert (2015) explicitly observes equal fixation probability but unequal conditional times on the 12-vertex regular Frucht graph, establishing the qualitative possibility as prior art.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The theorem was recast as whether same-degree vertices have equal conditional mean fixation time at a specified graph order; the reproductive-value formula alone gives success probabilities and no such equality of conditional time. The searched comparable results do not assert the all-five-vertex classification. The known twelve-vertex Frucht example does not imply that five is a sharp minimum or classify the first finite graph order.
searches: "same fixation probability" "conditional fixation time" Moran graph

evidence: The 2014 paper explicitly compares graphs through four vertices.
The 2019 graph atlas computes many graph-level observables, with no inspected table of within-graph same-degree mutant seeds and their conditional mean times.
A full graph census was independently generated for the candidate by exact rational Markov linear systems, producing canonical masks 29, 58, 62, 185, 187, 221, 254.
McAvoy–Hauert Appendix C tabulates Frucht-graph (12-vertex) absorption times at r=2; no five-vertex neutral conditional-time table is present in the inspected material.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No inspected table reports the seven of 21 split, its canonical graph representatives, or the paired P5 rational times. Database coverage is incomplete, so this is not a guarantee against uncatalogued or supplemental data.

originality.rationale: Prior sources establish neutral inverse-degree fixation probabilities, general Markov recursions and explicit non-equivalence of conditional fixation times for equal-probability seeds on the 12-vertex regular Frucht graph (McAvoy–Hauert, 2015). The new claim is restricted to sharp order five and the exact seven-of-21 class census, neither asserted nor implied by the inspected prior observations and methods. Priority is a best-evidence provisional assessment, not historical certainty.
residual_risks: A previously published or unindexed raw vertex-resolved time table or supplemental dataset could subsume the seven-class census without matching title language.
Not every section or supplement of every plausible paper was accessible or independently reviewed; full priority remains subject to outside historical examination.
Modern graph atlases with generic exact algorithms could have machine-generated but unpublished equivalent statistics.

value.rationale: The precise motivation is whether equality of reproductive value, which is sufficient to predict a neutral mutant’s success chance, is also sufficient to predict the expected time of successful fixation. The sharp transition at five vertices and full first census layer (seven of 21 graph classes) give a natural structural boundary and reproducible comparative benchmark. It is not merely a random small numeric example or a rebranding of a standard probability formula.
